questions.subject: science
questions.question: In which group do elements having electronic configuration 1s2, 2s2, 2p1 lie?
questions.explanation: This configuration has three valence electrons. Elements with three valence electrons are kept in group IIIA.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the elements between groups IIA and IIIA called in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Transition metals are placed between group IIA and group IIIA. So the d-block is in the middle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which one of the given nonmetals is the most reactive?
questions.explanation: Halogen reactivity decreases down the group. Fluorine is at the top, so it is most reactive.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which one of the given metals is the most reactive?
questions.explanation: Alkali metal reactivity increases down the group. Cesium is lower among these, so it is most reactive.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which group do inert gases belong to in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Noble gases are also called inert gases. They are kept in group 0.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which one represents the correct order of increase in chemical reactivity of metals?
questions.explanation: Metallic reactivity increases down a group. So the order is Be < Mg < Ca.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In the given periodic table positions A, B, C and D, which element can form acidic oxide?
questions.explanation: Nonmetals form acidic oxides. Nonmetals are placed toward the right side of the periodic table.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many elements have been discovered according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: There are 118 discovered elements. Among them, 92 are natural and 26 are artificial.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many naturally occurring elements are mentioned?
questions.explanation: There are 92 natural elements. The remaining 26 are artificial elements.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a periodic table?
options: A scientific table for studying elements by grouping similar properties
questions.explanation: Periodic table is a scientific table used to study elements. It arranges elements in order.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Who created a periodic table on the basis of atomic weight?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic weight. Moseley arranged them by atomic number.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does Mendeleev’s periodic law relate properties of elements to?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev's law is based on atomic weight. Modern periodic law is based on atomic number.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Who discovered that properties of elements depend on atomic number?
questions.explanation: Moseley showed atomic number is more basic. Mendeleev had used atomic weight.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does modern periodic law state?
options: Elements are arranged by colour only
Properties depend only on atomic weight
All elements have the same properties
Properties of elements are periodic functions of atomic number
questions.explanation: Modern periodic law is based on atomic number. Elements are arranged by increasing atomic number.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many periods are in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Modern periodic table has 7 periods and 18 groups. Periods are horizontal rows.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many groups are in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Modern periodic table has 18 groups. Seven is the number of periods.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are vertical columns in the periodic table called?
questions.explanation: Vertical columns are called groups. Horizontal rows are called periods.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are horizontal rows in the periodic table called?
questions.explanation: Horizontal rows are called periods. Vertical columns are called groups.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where are metals placed in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Metals are mostly on the left side. Nonmetals are on the right and metalloids are in the middle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where are nonmetals placed in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Nonmetals are placed on the right side. Metals are placed on the left side.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are isotopes?
options: Forms of the same element having different atomic weights
questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element. They have different atomic weights.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why was atomic weight not enough for the periodic table?
options: Isotopes of the same element have different atomic weights
questions.explanation: If atomic weight were used, isotopes would need separate places. Atomic number solves this problem.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is an orbit or shell?
options: Path in which electrons revolve around the nucleus
questions.explanation: A shell is the path around the nucleus where electrons move. It is an energy level.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which subshell is found in the K shell?
questions.explanation: K shell has only the 1s subshell. So 1s is its subshell.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the maximum number of electrons in s subshell?
questions.explanation: The s subshell can hold 2 electrons. p, d and f can hold more electrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the maximum number of electrons in p subshell?
questions.explanation: The p subshell can hold 6 electrons. That is its maximum capacity.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is Aufbau’s principle about?
options: Electrons fill subshells in increasing order of energy
Metals are always on the right side
questions.explanation: Aufbau's principle tells how electrons fill subshells. Lower energy subshells fill first.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which elements are called alkali metals?
options: Group IA elements like Li, Na and K
questions.explanation: Group IA elements are alkali metals. Halogens are in VIIA and inert gases are in group 0.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the valence shell electronic configuration of group IA elements?
questions.explanation: Group IA elements have one valence electron. So ns1 is their outer configuration.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which elements are called alkaline earth metals?
options: Group IIA elements such as Mg and Ca
questions.explanation: Mg and Ca are group IIA elements. Group IIA elements are alkaline earth metals.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which elements are called halogens?
options: Group VIIA elements like F, Cl, Br and I
questions.explanation: Group VIIA elements are called halogens. They have seven valence electrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are noble gases called inert gases?
options: They have a complete valence shell and do not take part in reactions
questions.explanation: Noble gases have a stable octet. So they are very less reactive.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are metalloids?
options: Elements showing some properties of metals and some of nonmetals
questions.explanation: Metalloids lie between metals and nonmetals. They show mixed properties.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does atomic size change from left to right in a period?
questions.explanation: Across a period, nuclear charge increases. So electrons are pulled more strongly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does atomic size decrease across a period?
options: New shells are added every step
Electrons are added in the same shell while nuclear attraction increases
questions.explanation: More protons increase nuclear attraction. So same-shell electrons are pulled more strongly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does atomic size change from top to bottom in a group?
questions.explanation: New shells are added down a group. So atomic size increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is electropositivity?
options: Property of gaining electrons to form anions
Property of losing valence electrons to form cations
Property of forming only digital signals
questions.explanation: Electropositivity means tendency to lose electrons. Losing electrons forms positive ions.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is electronegativity?
options: Property of gaining electrons to form anions
Property of losing electrons to form cations
questions.explanation: Electronegativity means tendency to gain electrons. It helps form negative ions.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does metallic character change from left to right in a period?
options: It changes into inert gas only
questions.explanation: Metallic character decreases across a period. Nonmetallic character increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does nonmetallic character change from left to right in a period?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period. Atoms attract electrons more strongly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does electropositivity change down a group?
questions.explanation: Down a group, atoms become larger. Larger atoms lose electrons more easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does electronegativity change down a group?
questions.explanation: Down a group, electrons are farther from the nucleus. So gaining electrons becomes harder.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does chemical reactivity of metals change down a group?
options: It is not related to atomic size
questions.explanation: Larger metal atoms lose valence electrons easily. So metallic reactivity increases down the group.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does chemical reactivity of nonmetals change down a group?
options: It becomes equal to zero always
questions.explanation: Down a nonmetal group, atom size increases. So gaining electrons becomes harder and reactivity decreases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which element is the most reactive metal in the third period example?
questions.explanation: In the third period, sodium is the most electropositive metal. So it is the most reactive metal there.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which element is the most reactive nonmetal in the third period example?
questions.explanation: In the third period, chlorine is the most electronegative reactive nonmetal. Argon is inert, so chlorine is chosen.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches group and common name?
questions.explanation: Group VIIA contains halogens. Fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine are halogens.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the general valency pattern across groups IA to 0 stated in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Valency changes across groups in a pattern. From IA to 0, it becomes 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are elements of the same group similar?
options: They are always in the same period
They have the same atomic weight only
They have similar valence shell electronic configuration
questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same valence electrons. So they show similar properties.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which electronic configuration belongs to chlorine as given in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Chlorine has seven valence electrons. Its outer configuration ends in 3p5.
